clue.text: Short skirt pretty girl's about to make shorter

indicators.note: the word about here means one piece wraps around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive girl; the 's stands for is
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Someone wants a pretty girl's miniskirt taken up even further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl's' reads as 'girl is', so the pretty girl is the container, not the wearer of the skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to reduce or lessen it, cutting it down in size.

clue.text: I take road transport to America, he tried flying

parts.note: a car is a vehicle used on roads
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A traveller describes driving to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wings of wax and feathers made by his father Daedalus, and fell when he flew too near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth famous for his doomed attempt at flight with waxen wings.

clue.text: Bill is a first name

parts.note: taken as written
AC is the abbreviation for account, and an account is a bill

explanation.surface: A statement that someone called Bill uses that as his forename.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like the person's name, but it is an account; it comes last in the answer though first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a Christian name, the kind given before a surname.

clue.text: Item I made can be produced without delay

indicators.note: the letters of these words can be worked into a new form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A craftsman promises an item he made can be delivered at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immediate happens instantly, at once and on the spot.

clue.text: They may rise up in anger

definitions.text: They may rise up in anger

parts.words: They may rise up in anger
parts.note: the neck feathers of a bird or hairs of an animal bristle when it is angry, and the idiom of getting one's back up follows

explanation.definitionFit: Raised neck feathers or hair are the classic sign of an animal, or person, growing angry.

clue.text: Concerning a light yellow check

parts.note: re means about or concerning
buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A remark about a pale yellow pattern of squares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like a fabric pattern going with the colour, but it is the definition, a verb meaning to repulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to rebuke or turn back, which is to check an advance.

clue.text: Two kings embracing are not seen so often

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (rex), so two kings give two Rs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Royal pairs are said to be seldom spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer occurs less frequently, so is met with less often.

clue.text: Miserable informer mown down in Kentucky?

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling miserable
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A gloomy snitch gets cut down somewhere in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASS is British slang for an informer. Kentucky is the Bluegrass State, named after a kind of meadow grass that is mown there.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow grass typical of Kentucky, cut like any lawn; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: It's possible a belief's been shaken

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that a conviction may have been rocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasible means practicable, able to be done.

clue.text: Mother gets involved with plan for making bombs

indicators.note: involved means mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother is caught up in a plot to make explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied incendiary used as the filling of fire bombs.

clue.text: A roundabout way to get a letter

definitions.meaning: indirect, going round in a circle
a printed notice sent out to many people at once

explanation.surface: Advice on an indirect way of receiving post.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundabout as an adjective means ring-shaped or indirect, and a mailshot sent to many recipients is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Drink calmed us when upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink soothed someone after they were upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: I am seen in unusual anger, but recover possession

indicators.note: seen in means put inside, so one piece goes within the other
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to strange anger yet gets their property back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns ANGER into REGAN, and 'seen in' puts I inside, after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain is to get back something lost.

clue.text: Change sides

parts.note: a coin, or loose change, has two faces, and the phrase names them as a call when tossing it

explanation.definitionFit: The two faces of a coin are what is called when it is tossed.

clue.text: People are known to hit them

definitions.text: People are known to hit them

parts.words: People are known to hit them
parts.note: someone becoming famous is said to hit the front pages, so the striking is a news idiom

explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the front-page titles is the idiom for becoming big news.

clue.text: See danger getting involved with traitors

indicators.note: becoming entangled means the letters are mixed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots peril in mixing with turncoats.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegades are deserters who abandon their side, much like turncoats.

clue.text: Succeed to some degree

parts.note: partly successful in ordinary reading, but really winning a university qualification

explanation.definitionFit: To pass out of university with a BA or similar is to win an academic degree.

clue.text: As in pre-stage make-up?

indicators.note: made up means formed anew, so the letters are rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Actors apply this before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' signals the anagram and the whole clue also describes theatrical cosmetics put on before a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical cosmetics worn by actors are applied before they go on stage.

clue.text: Cut down a dentist's work

parts.note: a bridge is a set of false teeth fitted by a dentist

explanation.surface: A dentist's handiwork is trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it.

clue.text: He holds listeners in a kind of transport

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: A man has people listening while travelling in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is a vehicle carrying a coffin to a funeral.

clue.text: Confused tot given guidance

parts.note: to tot up is to add
led means guided

explanation.surface: A bewildered toddler is shown the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child, but it is a verb, as in tot up, meaning sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Incredible fiddle shown up in this boardgame

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a Strad, a Stradivarius violin, is a famously fine fiddle

explanation.surface: A superb violin is put on display in a pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub game of throwing small arrows at a round board.

clue.text: Unusual regret about one's record

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I and the 's is is, together I and S

explanation.surface: A strange regret haunts someone's past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' turns REGRET into REGTER, which goes 'about' IS (one's, read as one is).
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official written list, a log of entries.

clue.text: Cuttlefish very good in water

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
pi is slang for pious, very good morally

explanation.surface: A cuttlefish behaves well in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the genus name of the cuttlefish, which also gives its name to the brown ink.

clue.text: New gardener brought in the crop

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly hired horticulturist harvested the produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnered means gathered and stored, as a harvest is.

clue.text: Turn out a bad citizen perhaps

definitions.text: Turn out a bad citizen perhaps

parts.words: Turn out a bad citizen perhaps
parts.note: expelling an undesirable from the country, with turn out sounding as if it means become

explanation.definitionFit: To expel an unwanted foreigner from a country by law.

clue.text: Those doing it are out for the count

definitions.text: Those doing it are out for the count

parts.words: Those doing it are out for the count
parts.note: out for the count usually means knocked unconscious, but here people are going round counting the population

explanation.definitionFit: An official count of a population, done by enumerators going door to door.

clue.text: Turn and sneer when trapped

indicators.note: turn means change, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone caught turns round and sneers at their captor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means caught in a snare or trap.
